cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does cloud security protect?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Cloud security protects cloud-based infrastructure, applications, services, identities and data from cyber threats.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which set lists common authentication factor types?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Authentication factors commonly include something you know, something you have and something you are.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Can you trust someone without giving them access to everything?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Yes. Trust can be gradual and specific. Someone may be a good friend without needing your passwords, private messages or financial information.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which use of money feels most valuable to you?
cards.subtitle: Choose the response closest to your value.

meta.source_reference: Saving for adversity and proper use of wealth

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What can authorized network scanning help identify?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Scanning can identify active hosts, exposed ports and available services. A port scanner specifically checks which network ports appear open or reachable.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Clear communication
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Clear communication states the purpose, important facts and requested next action without unnecessary ambiguity.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: If suspicious online activity affects you, report it to an appropriate trusted person or authority.
cards.subtitle: A tiny action linked to this idea.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What is the first priority in an emergency?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: In an emergency, personal safety comes first; follow local emergency guidance and seek trained help rather than taking unsafe risks.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: When should cloud data be protected with encryption?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: At rest and in transit when appropriate

cards.explain: Cloud data should be protected both at rest and in transit when appropriate, helping protect stored information and data moving across networks.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why is cybersecurity an ongoing process?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: Technology, vulnerabilities and attacks keep changing
One security product permanently stops every threat

cards.explain: Cybersecurity must continue adapting because technology, vulnerabilities, attackers and attack techniques continually change.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does a malicious backdoor bypass?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: A backdoor provides a way to bypass normal authentication or security mechanisms. Attackers may install one to maintain access after compromising a system.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Check that the software on your device is kept updated.
cards.subtitle: A tiny action linked to this idea.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Is all adware equally harmful?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: No. Adware displays unwanted advertising and may track activity, but not all adware is equally harmful. Malicious or intrusive adware can create security and privacy risks.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why can fileless malware challenge file-based detection?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: It relies heavily on tools, scripts, or memory

cards.explain: Fileless malware relies heavily on legitimate system tools, scripts, or memory rather than conventional malicious executable files stored on disk, making some file-based detection less effective.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why might a cybercriminal create a fake social-media profile?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Cybercriminals may create fake social-media profiles to impersonate other people. A familiar name or photo alone does not guarantee an account is genuine.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Protect the password that protects your password manager.
cards.subtitle: A tiny action linked to this idea.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What can Network Access Control restrict?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Network Access Control can restrict network access based on user, device or security requirements.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does network security protect?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Network security protects networks, connected devices and transmitted data from unauthorized access, misuse, modification and disruption.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Use a different password for each important account.
cards.subtitle: A tiny action linked to this idea.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: A friend tells you something private but not dangerous. What would you prefer to do?
cards.subtitle: Choose the response closest to your value.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: How large is a SHA-256 hash value?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: SHA-256 produces a 256-bit hash value.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Before sending one emotional message, reread it once.
cards.subtitle: A tiny action linked to this idea.

meta.source_reference: Balanced mind and restraint as valued qualities

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why should you be cautious with an unknown QR code?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: It may lead to a malicious site

cards.explain: QR codes can direct users to malicious or fake websites. Avoid scanning codes that are unknown or suspicious.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which common password attacks can passkeys reduce?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Passkeys can significantly reduce traditional phishing and credential-stuffing risks because they do not rely on a reusable website password.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What is malvertising?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Malvertising uses malicious or compromised online advertisements as part of an attack.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Can asking for help be a responsible decision?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Asking for help can be responsible when you recognize that support is needed instead of pretending you can handle everything alone.

meta.source_reference: Asking for help can be a responsible decision.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which information is safest to keep private online?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Your address is sensitive personal information. Share personal details online only when necessary and appropriate.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Money basics
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: A simple budget separates income, needs, wants, saving and planned spending.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why should important backups be tested?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: To confirm data can actually be restored

cards.explain: Backups can support recovery after incidents or failures, but testing is important to confirm that the stored data can actually be restored.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What is a botnet?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: A botnet is a network of compromised devices that attackers can remotely control. Botnets are frequently used to generate DDoS traffic and perform other malicious activities.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.topic_name: Encryption at rest and in transit
cards.title: Which type protects data while it moves between systems?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Encryption in transit protects information while it moves between systems. Encryption at rest protects stored information such as data on disks or in databases.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does catfishing mean online?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Catfishing involves using a false online identity to deceive someone. A convincing profile does not automatically prove who is behind it.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which download deserves extra caution?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: An unknown file from a suspicious site

cards.explain: Unknown files from suspicious websites may be unsafe. Students should avoid downloading them.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which approach gives account security several layers?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: Unique credentials plus MFA and secure recovery

cards.explain: Modern account security combines protections such as unique credentials, password managers, MFA, passkeys, secure recovery and breach monitoring rather than relying on passwords alone.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Check that you are not sharing a password with friends or classmates.
cards.subtitle: A tiny action linked to this idea.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does cybersecurity protect?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Cybersecurity protects computers, networks, applications, systems and data from digital attacks.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: A website uses HTTPS. What can you safely conclude?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: HTTPS encrypts communication with a website, but it does not prove that the website itself is trustworthy.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: How does a worm differ from a traditional virus?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: It must attach to another program

cards.explain: A worm can spread automatically across vulnerable systems or networks and generally does not need to attach itself to another program.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What is cryptography?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Cryptography is the science of protecting information using mathematical techniques.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What can a web proxy help an authorized tester examine?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: A web proxy can let an authorized tester inspect and modify HTTP requests and responses during web-application security testing.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Make sure you know how to contact a trusted adult in an emergency.
cards.subtitle: A tiny action linked to this idea.

meta.source_reference: Preparation for adversity and importance of reliable support

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Keep water available during your next study session.
cards.subtitle: A tiny action linked to nutrition.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which device forwards packets between different IP networks?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: A router forwards packets between different IP networks. A switch typically connects devices within a network and forwards Ethernet frames using MAC addresses.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What is your digital footprint?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: A digital footprint is the trail of information associated with your online activities. It can influence your online reputation.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What should responsible borrowers understand?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Responsible borrowing requires understanding the obligation to repay what is borrowed.

meta.source_reference: Responsible borrowing requires understanding repayment obligations.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Where is it safer to practise offensive cybersecurity techniques?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: CTFs and security labs provide intentionally vulnerable or controlled environments for practice, unlike real systems that you do not have permission to test.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What can a Remote Access Trojan enable?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: A Remote Access Trojan, or RAT, can give an attacker remote control over an infected device.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Does every unfinished plan need to be announced?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: No. Some plans benefit from quiet preparation. Share when collaboration, safety or feedback requires it, not simply for attention.

meta.source_reference: Verse advising discretion about intended actions

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What is special about phishing-resistant MFA?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Phishing-resistant MFA helps prevent users from authenticating to fraudulent websites. Hardware security keys can provide strong phishing-resistant authentication.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does a basic budget help you track?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: A budget helps track money coming in as income and money going out as expenses.

meta.source_reference: Money management is an important life skill; a budget helps track income and expenses.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which two hashes are unsuitable for modern collision-resistant security uses?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: MD5 is cryptographically broken, and SHA-1 is also considered unsuitable for modern applications that require collision resistance.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Is a strong encryption algorithm enough by itself?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: No. Modern cryptographic security also depends on secure implementations, sufficient key sizes, good randomness, careful key management and correct protocol design.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What protects HTTPS communications?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: HTTPS protects HTTP communications using TLS. TLS helps provide confidentiality, integrity and authentication for network communications.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does Zero Trust continuously evaluate?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Zero Trust principles can continuously evaluate identity, device, context and access requirements when controlling access to cloud resources.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Digital security
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Strong unique passwords and multi-factor authentication reduce the risk that one stolen credential compromises multiple accounts.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which key generally creates a digital signature?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Digital signatures are generally created with a private key. The corresponding public key can then be used to verify the signature.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does signature-based malware detection compare?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: Only the age of a file

cards.explain: Traditional signature-based detection identifies malware by comparing content with known malicious patterns.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does a digital certificate connect?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: A digital certificate associates an identity or domain name with a public key. Certificate Authorities issue and sign certificates within a Public Key Infrastructure.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: How is an exploit related to a vulnerability?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: A vulnerability is a weakness. An exploit is a technique or code that takes advantage of that weakness.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: A useful message should make clear…
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: What you need and by when

cards.explain: Clear communication states the purpose, important facts and requested next action without unnecessary ambiguity.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Is configuring backups enough for reliable recovery?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Backups can support recovery from ransomware, accidental deletion and service failures, but recovery procedures should also be regularly tested.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why should an unexpected email attachment make you cautious?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Suspicious email attachments can contain malware. Treat unexpected attachments cautiously rather than assuming they are safe.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why do authorized testers enumerate exposed services?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Service enumeration gathers additional information about exposed services. Banner information can sometimes reveal the service software or its version.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: A phishing attempt arrives by SMS. What is it called?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Smishing is phishing through SMS or text messages. Vishing is phishing through phone or voice calls.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which capability may an NGFW provide beyond traditional filtering?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: A Next-Generation Firewall can add capabilities beyond traditional filtering, including application awareness and intrusion prevention.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What is phishing designed to do?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Phishing uses fake messages or websites to steal information. The message may pretend to come from a trusted bank, school, company or other organization.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why are network logs useful after a security incident?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Network logs provide records that can help teams investigate security incidents and troubleshoot problems.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why do organizations need cybersecurity policies?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Cybersecurity policies establish rules and responsibilities for protecting an organization's systems and information.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does “स्वच्छता” mean?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: स्वच्छता (svacchatā) means “cleanliness.” The source connects cleanliness with health.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Conflict resolution
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Constructive conflict resolution separates the problem from the person and looks for needs, facts and workable next steps.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Pause once today and name what you are feeling.
cards.subtitle: A tiny action linked to this idea.

meta.source_reference: Emotional awareness helps people understand their feelings.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What do strong passwords help protect?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Strong passwords help protect online accounts from unauthorized access.

meta.source_reference: Strong passwords help protect online accounts.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What role does a cryptographic key play?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: A cryptographic key is a value used by an algorithm to protect or recover information. Modern cryptography generally depends on protecting keys rather than hiding the algorithms.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: You receive repeated login approvals you didn't request. What should you do?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: MFA fatigue attacks repeatedly send approval requests hoping a victim accepts one. Unexpected authentication requests should be rejected and investigated.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What is safer for two important accounts?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Important accounts should use different passwords. Reusing one password can put multiple accounts at risk if that password is exposed.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does ransomware commonly do?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Ransomware prevents or restricts access to systems or data and demands payment. Many variants encrypt files to make them inaccessible.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: When emotions are intense, what usually improves a decision?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Chanakya praises a balanced mind. In modern situations, giving yourself thinking space can reduce impulsive decisions.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: How does RBAC assign permissions?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Role-Based Access Control assigns permissions according to defined roles, helping organize which identities receive which access rights.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which is the best next action?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: Solve five practice questions at 6 PM

cards.explain: Useful goals connect a meaningful outcome with measurable progress and a clear next action.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which password habit is safest?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Strong unique passwords and multi-factor authentication reduce the risk that one stolen credential compromises multiple accounts.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: A system works when authorized users need it. Which goal is this?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Availability means systems and information remain accessible when authorized users need them.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Turn on multi-factor authentication for one important account.
cards.subtitle: A tiny action linked to digital security.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why might malware use obfuscation or packing?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Malware may use obfuscation, encryption, or packing to conceal parts of its code or make its behavior harder to analyze.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does active listening mean?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Active listening means paying careful attention to another person rather than simply waiting for your turn to speak.

meta.source_reference: Active listening means paying careful attention to others.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does web security protect?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Web security protects websites, web applications, APIs, users and data from cyber threats.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: How can planning help with a difficult task?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Planning can make a difficult task easier to manage by helping you organize what needs to be done.

meta.source_reference: Planning can make difficult tasks easier to manage.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Does digitally signing data necessarily encrypt it?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Digital signatures can verify authenticity and integrity, but signing information does not necessarily encrypt the signed data.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why is a zero-day vulnerability especially challenging?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Defenders have had no time, or effectively no opportunity, to deploy a fix before exploitation becomes possible or occurs.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why schedule a start time?
cards.subtitle: Connect time management to the way you think or act.

options.label: Yes — I want to explore this

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Check whether your device has pending security updates.
cards.subtitle: A tiny action linked to this idea.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why is keeping software updated an online-safety habit?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Operating systems, browsers and applications should be kept updated because updates often include important security fixes.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Should passwords generally use fast general-purpose hashes?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: No. Passwords should generally be processed with dedicated password-hashing or key-derivation algorithms rather than fast general-purpose hashes.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which supports everyday nutrition?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Balanced eating includes appropriate amounts of diverse foods, hydration and attention to individual needs.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What is a safer habit for live-location sharing?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: Share it publicly all the time
Share only with a clear reason

cards.explain: Avoid sharing your live location publicly unless there is a clear reason. Location information deserves the same thoughtful privacy decisions as other personal information.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does spyware do?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Spyware is malware that secretly collects information about a device or its user.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does OSINT mean in cybersecurity?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Open-Source Intelligence means collecting information from publicly available sources such as search engines, public records, websites and public code repositories.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Check whether your device and browser have pending security updates.
cards.subtitle: A tiny action linked to this idea.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why can MFA strengthen an account?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: It requires more than one authentication factor

cards.explain: Multi-factor authentication requires more than one authentication factor, adding another security check beyond a single factor.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: An app asks for permissions it does not seem to need. What is the safer response?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: Consider whether each permission is appropriate

cards.explain: Be cautious when apps request unnecessary permissions. Camera, microphone, contacts and location access should be granted only when appropriate.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Treat OTPs and authentication codes as sensitive information.
cards.subtitle: A tiny action linked to this idea.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: A student is experiencing serious online harassment. Which response can help?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: Tell a trusted adult or teacher

cards.explain: For serious online harassment, students should consider telling a trusted adult, teacher or appropriate authority. Blocking and reporting tools can also help with abusive accounts.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does access control determine?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: Who can access resources and what they can do

cards.explain: Access control determines which users or systems can access particular resources and what actions they may perform.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why does MFA help?
cards.subtitle: Connect digital security to the way you think or act.

options.label: Yes — I want to explore this

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which malware disguises itself as legitimate or desirable software?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: A Trojan horse hides malicious functionality behind software that appears legitimate or desirable.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Check that an important school or personal document has a safe backup.
cards.subtitle: A tiny action linked to this idea.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which is the strongest overall malware-defense approach?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: Rely on one security tool only

cards.explain: Effective malware defense combines layers such as patching, endpoint protection, secure configuration, backups, access controls, network monitoring, and user awareness.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which malware can spread without attaching itself to another program?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: A worm can spread between vulnerable systems without attaching itself to another program. A virus typically spreads when its host file or program is executed.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which can be a route for malware infection?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Malware can spread through malicious email attachments. Malicious or compromised websites can also be used to distribute malware.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Before opening an unexpected link, stop and check it first.
cards.subtitle: A tiny action linked to this idea.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does “उत्तरदायित्वम्” mean?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: उत्तरदायित्वम् (uttaradāyitvam) means “responsibility.” The source encourages taking responsibility for one's actions.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What is one security benefit of network segmentation?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Network segmentation can reduce unnecessary communication between cloud resources. Firewalls, security groups and network policies can further restrict traffic.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why can an unexpected shortened link deserve extra caution?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Shortened links can hide their final destination. When one arrives unexpectedly, open it cautiously rather than assuming the visible short link is safe.
